draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Thalassery! The British built this fort in 1708 to guard their pepper trade. The town also claims some of Kerala's firsts: cricket, cake and the circus.
draft.hungryLine: Thalassery biryani is made with small, fragrant kaima rice, not basmati. You have to try it here.

moodReplies.show-me-around: See the fort, then walk to Gundert Bungalow, where the first Malayalam-English dictionary was written.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Drive 15 minutes to Muzhappilangad, where you can drive along the beach itself.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Kerala's first bakery cake is said to have been baked in Thalassery in 1883, for a British planter's Christmas.

legends.title: Kerala's first cake
legends.body: A baker named Mambally Bapu is said to have baked Kerala's first cake in 1883, after a planter showed him a cake from England.

legends.title: The cradle of Indian circus
legends.body: Keeleri Kunhikannan trained gymnasts here, and Thalassery became the cradle of Indian circus.

tips.title: Drive the beach at low tide.
tips.body: Check the tide and stay on firm sand.

tips.title: Buy cake at the old bakeries.
tips.body: Plum cake is a local favourite, especially at Christmas.

story.title: A pepper station
story.body: The English East India Company set up a trading post here to buy pepper and cardamom.

story.title: The fort
story.body: The Company built Thalassery Fort to protect its trade.

story.title: A dictionary
story.body: Hermann Gundert, a German missionary, settled here and later wrote a Malayalam-English dictionary.

story.title: Cake, circus and cricket
story.body: A bakery, the first circus troupes, and cricket played by the British made Thalassery famous.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Fort, biryani, then the drive-in beach at sunset. Tell me if the biryani lived up to it.
